closest.title: Globally-Robust Neural Networks
closest.how_close: Closest methodological match: GloRo uses global Lipschitz bounds and output margins for inexpensive inference-time certification, with an abstention output when certification fails. It targets image classification and incorporates robust training; it does not evaluate EEG command gating, SDP bounds, or BCI-controlled effectors.

closest.title: A Formally Verified Robustness Certifier for Neural Networks
closest.how_close: Precomputes and caches margin Lipschitz bounds, then checks each prediction by comparing logit differences with the perturbation budget times those bounds. This closely matches the proposed offline-bound/online-margin computation. Its contribution is a verified certifier for dense ReLU networks, evaluated on image models, rather than BCI runtime abstention.

closest.title: From confidence to caution: conformal gating for cross-session motor imagery brain-computer interfaces
closest.how_close: Closest target and intervention: withholds uncertain motor-imagery BCI commands and evaluates decision rates, wrong-command rates, and risk-weighted utility under session shift. Uses conformal prediction and selective prediction rather than Lipschitz-margin robustness certificates.

closest.title: When Certificates Fail: A Unified Safety Framework for Embedded Neural Interface Models
closest.how_close: This preprint evaluates EEG decoder safety using layerwise Lipschitz bounds, logit-margin certified-safe fractions, PGD attacks, and physiological stress tests, including EEGNet and MOABB-supported data. It is an offline safety audit; it does not implement certificate-triggered abstention or closed-loop effector command suppression.

closest.title: Degradation Attacks on Certifiably Robust Neural Networks
closest.how_close: Studies runtime defenses that reject inputs when local robustness cannot be certified, including Lipschitz-based GloRo models. Demonstrates adversarially induced unnecessary rejection. The certificate-to-rejection mechanism overlaps strongly, but the target is general image classifiers and the contribution concerns attacks on availability.

closest.title: Certifiers Make Neural Networks Vulnerable to Availability Attacks
closest.how_close: Explicitly studies a model-certifier-fallback pipeline that abstains whenever robustness cannot be guaranteed. Establishes prior use of certification as an operational gate, but evaluates availability attacks against general classifiers rather than Lipschitz-margin monitoring of EEG-driven effectors.

rationale: Very close work exists, but I found no outside-bibliography paper implementing the complete BCI certificate-to-abstention monitor. The generic mechanism is established: [GloRo](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/leino21a.html) combines Lipschitz bounds, margins, runtime certification, and abstention, while the [verified certifier](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06958) closely matches precomputation followed by per-output margin checks. The target also has close precedents: [conformal BCI gating](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42805221/) suppresses uncertain commands using a different technique, and [When Certificates Fail](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06630) evaluates Lipschitz-margin certification on EEG without deploying an abstention gate. Thus the apparent remaining contribution is applying and evaluating an established certification-gating mechanism for BCI effectors, particularly its comparison with adversarial detectors and closed-loop unsafe-command measurements. These are substantial overlaps, but none establishes the same target, intervention, and technique together.
